claims.text: Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni alloys can contain a fine lamellar microstructure of alternating soft FCC and hard, ordered B2 phases.
The proposed fine lamellar architecture is self-organized.
The B2 phase in the lamellar architecture is enriched in Al and Ni.
Tailored thermo-mechanical processing can produce or retain a refined lamellar duplex microstructure in AlCoCrFeNi2.1.
Maintenance of the fine FCC/B2 lamellar architecture is the critical factor governing phase stability.
The lamellar architecture stabilizes the phase distribution against coarsening.
The lamellar architecture stabilizes the alloy against environment-induced degradation.
The lamellar architecture contributes to retaining high-temperature mechanical performance.
The lamellar architecture contributes to retaining radiation tolerance.
The lamellar architecture contributes to retaining cryogenic toughness.
The lamellar structure restricts diffusion under thermal and environmental stress.
The lamellar structure impedes phase coarsening under thermal and environmental stress.
The Al/Ni-enriched B2 phase promotes oxidation resistance.
The B2 phase acts as a barrier to radiation damage.
The ductile FCC matrix supports toughness specifically at cryogenic temperatures.
Relative to an as-cast baseline, processed lamellar samples will show minimal coarsening and stable phase fractions after prolonged high-temperature exposure.
Relative to an as-cast baseline, processed lamellar samples will exhibit superior corrosion and oxidation resistance with more stable passive films.
Relative to an as-cast baseline, processed lamellar samples will retain higher yield strength and fracture toughness after radiation exposure.
Relative to an as-cast baseline, processed lamellar samples will exhibit improved cryogenic ductility.
As-cast or conventionally processed Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni baselines generally have coarse, inhomogeneous, or poorly defined lamellar microstructures.
